name: Ward–Hilton
question: For women undergoing first surgery for urodynamic stress incontinence, how does retropubic tension-free vaginal tape compare with colposuspension?

arms.label: colposuspension using each centre's standard technique

design.population: Women with urodynamic stress incontinence who had completed childbearing and were selected for first continence surgery at 14 UK and Irish centres.
design.description: Multicentre randomized comparative surgical trial; six-month primary report
design.locator: BMJ 2002 Methods, Table 1 and participant-flow figure

verdictNote: Six-month cure difference was nonsignificant; recruitment was insufficient to establish equivalence.
takeaway: Retropubic tension-free vaginal tape and colposuspension had 66% versus 57% six-month objective cure in first-surgery stress incontinence; the difference was not statistically significant. TVT shortened recovery but caused more bladder injuries, and the trial was too small to establish equivalence.

reports.label: Six-month randomized report
reports.citation: Ward K, Hilton P; UK and Ireland TVT Trial Group. "Prospective multicentre randomised trial of tension-free vaginal tape and colposuspension as primary treatment for stress incontinence." *BMJ.* 2002;325(7355):67. doi:10.1136/bmj.325.7355.67
reports.followUp: Six months after surgery; missing outcomes counted as failures in the randomized denominator
reports.followUpLocator: BMJ 2002 Methods and Results, participant-flow figure

results.measure: Six-month negative one-hour pad test plus negative cystometric stress test; risk difference in percentage points (TVT minus colposuspension)
results.note: Calculated raw risk difference is 8.3 percentage points; the article reports the confidence interval for the difference. A 10-point difference was prespecified as important, requiring 197 patients per arm for 80% power; the study was not powered to conclude equivalence.
Randomized denominator; narrower endpoint than combined objective cure.

harms.label: Bladder injury, including perforation or visible trauma
harms.note: Among women who underwent their allocated operation; P=0.013.

harms.label: Urinary tract infection within six weeks
Retropubic vascular injury requiring laparotomy and transfusion
harms.note: An anomalous obturator artery was injured during TVT.

delivery.label: Allocated operations performed
delivery.note: Preoperative withdrawal was more frequent after assignment to colposuspension.

delivery.label: Operative technique and anesthesia
delivery.value: TVT was placed by the Ulmsten technique under local anesthesia and sedation after surgeon training; colposuspension used each centre's standard technique with standardized suture number, suture material and postoperative catheterization, usually under general anesthesia.

delivery.label: Median return to normal activities
delivery.note: Patient-reported; participants knew their treatment assignment.

reports.label: Two-year update
reports.citation: Ward KL, Hilton P; UK and Ireland TVT Trial Group. "A prospective multicenter randomized trial of tension-free vaginal tape and colposuspension for primary urodynamic stress incontinence: two-year follow-up." *Am J Obstet Gynecol.* 2004;190(2):324-331. doi:10.1016/j.ajog.2003.07.029
reports.followUp: Two years; missing outcomes counted as treatment failures in the reported intention-to-treat analysis

results.measure: Two-year objective cure, defined as a negative one-hour pad test (less than 1 g weight change); participants with missing data counted as failures
results.note: Among women with data available at 24 months, a negative pad test was recorded in 111/137 (81%) after TVT and 86/108 (80%) after colposuspension (OR 1.09, 95% CI 0.59 to 2.06).

reports.label: Five-year extension
reports.citation: Ward KL, Hilton P; UK and Ireland TVT Trial Group. "Tension-free vaginal tape versus colposuspension for primary urodynamic stress incontinence: 5-year follow up." *BJOG.* 2008;115(2):226-233. doi:10.1111/j.1471-0528.2007.01548.x
reports.followUp: Five years; 98/175 TVT and 79/169 colposuspension participants reviewed, with pad tests in 72 and 49
reports.followUpLocator: BJOG PDF p2 and Figure 1, p3

results.measure: Five-year negative one-hour pad test, less than 1 g gain, among participants with available tests
results.note: Available-case odds ratio; the small tested subset limits inference.

results.endpoint: Negative one-hour pad test with last observation carried forward
results.measure: Five-year sensitivity analysis using last observed pad test for missing data
results.note: Imputation may conceal deterioration between the last visit and five years.

results.measure: Five-year BFLUTS patient-reported complete continence among questionnaire respondents
results.note: Different respondent denominator from the pad-test analysis.
results.locator: BJOG PDF p2, Secondary outcome measures

harms.label: Surgery for prolapse by five years
harms.note: Denominator is women who received allocated surgery; P=0.025.

harms.label: Further surgery for stress incontinence by five years
harms.note: P=0.74. The table prints 2.3% for 4/170, although direct calculation rounds to 2.4%.

harms.label: Tape-related complications by five years
harms.note: Three vaginal erosions, one obstruction requiring tape division, one suprapubic extrusion and one intravesical tape requiring cystotomy; three events were first detected at five years.

delivery.label: Five-year follow-up and pad-test availability
delivery.note: Only 11 of 14 original centres joined the extension.
